function.name: get_stock_data
function.description: Retrieve the most recent trading day's closing price and volume for a specified stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: The stock symbol of the company.

data_points.description: The type of data you want to retrieve for the stock. This can include closing price, opening price, volume, etc.

They want the most recent trading day's closing price and volume. We need to use the function get_stock_data. The function signature: get_stock_data takes symbol and data_points: "price" | "volume"[].

We need to call the function for each symbol. But the function expects data_points: "price" | "volume"[]? Actually data_points: "price" | "volume"[] means either "price" or an array of "volume"? We'll assume we can pass an array of strings: ["price", "volume"].

We need to call the function for each symbol. The symbols: Apple: AAPL, Google: GOOGL (or GOOG), Microsoft: MSFT. They are all listed on NASDAQ, not NYSE. But the user says "紐約證券交易所" (NYSE). Apple, Google, Microsoft are on NASDAQ. But maybe they want the data anyway. We'll just fetch the data.

We need to call the function for each symbol. We can combine calls? The function only accepts one symbol at a time. So we need to call three times. We'll produce three calls. But the system might want a single function call? The function signature only allows one symbol. So we need to call it three times. We'll do that.

We'll output the calls.
